## Active

### D-0004 — Migrations are code, applied by CI on merge; the Builder drafts additive and blocks risky

*2026-06-07 · scope: `supabase/migrations/**, .github/workflows/migrations.yml, agents/builder/**` · source: daemon STATUS 2026-06-07 and 2026-06-09; wmpc-meta/conventions/migrations.md*

**Decision.** Schema changes are drafted in a PR, reviewed, and applied by CI on merge to the
routed branch. No interactive session runs `supabase db push`. The Builder may draft additive
and reversible migrations (create table/index/view, nullable column, new enum value,
non-SECURITY-DEFINER function). It blocks destructive DDL, NOT NULL or UNIQUE on populated
columns, RLS and policies, SECURITY DEFINER, money, and backfills.

**Why.** Manual pushes caused wrong-project links and drift (tournament-manager #71, #77).
CI on merge gives one path with a review trail.

**Forbids.** `supabase db push` from a session or agent. A migration outside a PR.

### D-0005 — Branch work happens in a worktree; the pre-push guard keeps code off protected branches

*2026-06-08 · scope: `.git/hooks/pre-push, infrastructure/git-guards/**, infrastructure/worktrees/**` · source: daemon STATUS 2026-06-08; infrastructure/git-guards/DESIGN.md*

**Decision.** Every actor (interactive session, Builder, sync job) does branch work in its own
git worktree, never the shared main checkout. A `pre-push` hook installed by `reconcile.sh` in
every repo refuses a direct push of anything but the continuity allowlist (`STATUS.md`,
`activity/`, `DECISIONS.md`) to `main` or `production`. `WMPC_ALLOW_MAIN_PUSH=1` is the
deliberate override.

**Why.** Concurrent actors thrashed one checkout's HEAD and produced accidental direct-to-main
commits, in repos where a push to a routed branch deploys.

**Forbids.** Branch work in the shared checkout. Code or schema pushed to a protected branch
without a PR.

### D-0007 — main deploys TEST, production deploys PROD, promotion is a main-to-production PR

*2026-06-15 · scope: `.github/workflows/**, wrangler.*, DEPLOYMENT.md` · source: daemon STATUS 2026-06-15 (CORRECTION: main=TEST, production=PROD, daemon #39); wmpc-meta/conventions deploy-environments block*

**Decision.** In the branch-routed product repos a push to `main` applies to TEST (test
Supabase plus test Cloudflare) and a push to `production` applies to PROD. Promotion is a
GitHub `main` to `production` PR. A PR preview is a third environment with its own variable
scope and is not TEST.

**Known exceptions, by repo.** `wmpc-web` has no `production` branch and its `main` is the
live site, so nothing incomplete merges there. The mini-hosted repos have no `production`
branch and a push to `main` deploys nothing. Each repo's `DEPLOYMENT.md` YAML block is the
authority; parse it rather than inferring the shape.

**Why.** The first documentation of the model had it backwards. Getting this wrong is an
unreviewed prod deploy.

**Forbids.** Treating `main` as prod in a routed repo, or as inert in `wmpc-web`. Promoting
by local push instead of a PR.

### D-0008 — MCP wiring is generated from a committed project identity file

*2026-07-13 · scope: `.mcp.json, .wmpc-project.json, scripts/claude-bootstrap.sh` · source: daemon STATUS 2026-07-13 (DECIDED: self-healing MCP wiring); wmpc-meta PR #16*

**Decision.** Each repo commits `.wmpc-project.json` (`supabase.test_ref`, `supabase.prod_ref`,
`cloudflare.project`). `claude-bootstrap.sh` regenerates `.mcp.json` from it on every run.
Supabase gets full control on TEST and read-only on PROD, as two server entries. Cloudflare
uses account-wide servers. `connect-project.sh` discovers projects via the management APIs
with read-only tokens that are never committed or printed.

**Why.** Hand-wired MCP files drifted and one bug had rating-session-manager querying Third
Shot Academy's database through a shared project ref.

**Forbids.** Hand-editing `.mcp.json`. Committing management tokens. A write-capable PROD
Supabase MCP entry.

### D-0010 — Customer video is owned by rating-session-manager, served from the NAS behind an emailed code

*2026-08-26 · scope: `src/routes/videos.ts, **/video*/**, **/recordings/**` · source: daemon STATUS 2026-08-26 (later); rating-session-manager PR #61 (design, issue #60)*

**Decision.** rating-session-manager is the only repo that touches video. It already runs
Express on the mini with a Supabase service-role client, and club-dashboard is a backend-less
SPA that cannot serve files. Customers reach their videos through an emailed six-digit code,
not a magic link, on a download screen that shows only their sessions, with every access
logged and Third Shot Academy branding. Storage is on-site now (LAN off the NAS, `VIDEO_DIR`
pointed at the mount) and anywhere later (cloud). A grant expires after 30 days by default;
the file stays on the NAS.

**Why.** A magic link breaks on a LAN-only host when the phone fetches mail over cellular, and
link-preview scanners consume single-use links. The NAS path needs no code.

**Applies to.** Any lesson-recording, streaming, or video-delivery proposal. Extending
delivery to the cloud or to a streaming source is a supersession of this record, argued
against these reasons, not a fresh design.

**Forbids.** A second repo serving or storing customer video. A magic-link gate.

### D-0014 — Anything we build gives the Chief of Staff unattended access

*2026-09-14 · scope: `infrastructure/INFRA-INTAKE.md, agents/chief-of-staff/**, **/cos_whitelist*` · source: daemon STATUS 2026-09-14; daemon #100; wmpc-meta #25 (engineering-standard block v3)*

**Decision.** Every component that holds club data or does club work is reachable by the
Chief of Staff unattended: a documented entry point on the mini under the host guard, a
`wmpc-mcp` tool with read-only annotations for claude.ai and Cowork scheduled runs, and when
it acts, a `cos_whitelist` key plus the `cos_approvals` path for the gated part. This is
INFRA-INTAKE question 11 and part of the definition of done.

**Why.** qbo-api had a write transport for a week before the CoS could draft an invoice;
wmpc-mcp tools were auto-declined in a scheduled run because nothing marked them read-only.

**Forbids.** "Ron can do it from the dashboard" as the only surface.

### D-0016 — daemon is the architect of record; decisions live in a register and each repo carries its slice

*2026-09-16 · scope: `decisions/**, DECISIONS.md, NOW.md, .claude/hooks/session-start.sh, infrastructure/decision-register/**` · source: this change; Ron 2026-09-16 ("All decisions come through you. You're the architect.")*

**Decision.** Architectural decisions are records in `daemon/decisions/`, one file each, with an
ID, a status, the repos and paths they govern, the decision, the why, and what they forbid. A
decision is never deleted; a reversal is a new record that supersedes the old one. daemon holds
the full register. Every other repo carries `DECISIONS.md`, a generated slice of the records
that name it, published by daemon. `NOW.md` in daemon is the front door a session reads first;
`STATUS.md` stays the append-only log underneath it. A SessionStart hook prints the front door
and the index into every session's context, local or remote.

**Why.** STATUS.md had grown to eleven thousand lines. Decisions buried in it were invisible to
a fresh session, which could re-open something already settled. Repos need to see what binds
them without reading daemon. daemon needs to see everything.

**Forbids.** Recording a decision only in STATUS.md. Editing a superseded record instead of
adding a new one. Hand-editing a repo's `DECISIONS.md`.
